[quote=shahzada;59908703][b]Question of the Day #194:[/b]

Should a nation have laws that protect against discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, or should these issues be handled privately?

Nation Question: How would your nation handle this issue?

[i]This is an automated message.[/i][/quote]
No. There are already laws about assault, battery, murder, etc. It's only truly "discrimination", in my opinion, if it violates the law. So, if somebody tells a gay man that they should go to hell, the man that said that shouldn't go to jail unless he punches the gay man right after saying it. So, mostly, it should be handled privately. There is no reason to add a yapping charge. If you're offended womp womp imo.

As a nation, my government would disapprove and make any form of LGBT procedures and influence on minors illegal and punishable up to 4+ years in prison. For example, forcing a child or telling a child to be gay or trans would be considered child abuse [and sometimes, as a second charge child endangerment] in Stachelland. LGBT protests are illegal and are misdemeanors in Stachelland, punishable with community service, fines, probation, and suspended sentences. LGBT "propaganda" which varies, is a misdemeanor punished with fines and repeated offenses result in suspended sentences.

Putting up any form of LGBT flag is required to be taken down within 2 days or face a 200+ Stachell fine, and repeated offenses will result in immediate fines/jail time. LGBT marriage is allowed but closely monitored for the first few months.

[spoiler=The Grand Pantagrueli Dilemma]
[b]Bombardo, Pantagruel[/b]

[i]Kim Jung Un sits anxiously in his palace, today was supposed to be the day he delivered his speech addressing the Chambauza Gas Facility explosion, which was caused by his incompetency and the lack of funding for the economy in favour of the military. Though his time to loathe himself was interrupted, an official barges in with important news. 

"[b]Supreme Leader, I hate to be the bearer of bad news but the pursuit team sent to Replazum has been eliminated. The Federalist Coalition forces are still on the run[/b]." The official said hesitantly, he knew he was dead. Kim was infamous for killing those who bear bad news.

Immediately, Kim snapped his fingers, and two guards grabbed the man and dragged him out of the room, and as soon as the doors closed a loud gunshot echoed across the palace.

Kim looked down at the floor, the disappointment of his failures rested on his shoulders like a truck, Kim never felt this feeling before. He was always a proud man whose ambitions were seen to many as ludicrous. And they were right, he and his 200 year long dynasty had destroyed Pantagruel, turning the state from the powerhouse of Amarallo that it used to be to a pariah state which had no moral compass.

The boos of the crowd outside of the palace only grew louder, it was only driving Kim insane. He couldn't bear to look at the face of the disappointing people, malnourished and skinny, while he was fat and well fed. Kim never knew empathy, he never had to skip a day without a meal, he never had to work,  what made him was his father. He was nothing special, just a paranoid dictator who seemed to have no regrets on the outside, but was a little baby on the inside.

Then, another officer entered the room. 

"[b]The people are becoming impatient, what should we do Supreme Leader?[/b]"

Kim looked at him, then looked at the ground.

"[b]Arrest them, kill those who resist.[/b]"

The guard gasped, he couldn't understand what this man was saying. The shock, the horror, the cruelty of such an action was infuriating. But he had to swallow his disagreement, or he would face the same fat as his comrade.

"Allah, forgive me." He whispered to himself

[b]___________
[/b]

Farah and her mother were one among the millions who had come to Kim's palace in Bombardo to protest. Life had become survival, and food was a rarity. Farah was underweight, but Farah and her family weren't always like this. They used to be on a family care program issued by Kim Jung Un's predecessor,  Kim Jung Il. The program gave them monthly food rations that were barely enough to feed them. But recently, Kim had abolished the program in favour of increasing the budget of the military. Ever since then, Farah and her family have been living on the brink of starvation.

Millions swarmed the city bloc, chanting slurs and slogans against the government. A notable one that Farah had taken notice of was one talking about the Federation. What was the Federation?, she never knew as the speaking of politics was banned amongst women.

[b]Mother, every time we come out here to protest the guards always shoot at us. Why havent they done so now?[/b] Farah asked, her bony hands rubbing against her mothers gaunty figure. 

[b]I dont know, but this might be a step in the right direction. Maybe our voices can be finally heard.[/b] Her mother said weakly, the bellowing growl of her stomach interrupting her. 

Then the roars of gunshots interrupted them, the chanting of the crowd turned to screaming. And the horde dispersed in all directions trying to get to safety. But most of their efforts were in vain, bullets pierced the crowd from all directions and tank rounds filled the ground with craters of blood. This was nothing Farah had seen before, the soldiers always used dummy rounds and tear gas. But this, this was full on genocide.

Farah tried to run with her mom, but tripped over a dead body. Soon the horde began trampling all over her. 

[b]Mom! Mom![/b] Farah yelled in pain, but the snapping of a bone in her legs intrerrupted her screams and turned them into cries. Fortunetely, her cries did not fall to deaf ears. 15 minutes after the attacks began, the crowd had slowly cleared up and her mother came back for her. 

[b]Im so sorry Farah, please dont cry. Theyll hear u-[/b] 

The echoes of a gunshot ringed throughout the block, her mothers body thumped to the ground with a lifeless expression. Farah wanted to scream, but she couldnt. Theyd hear her, and if they did, shed be next.

In what felt like years the soldiers finally regrouped, and left the bodies to rot as a symbol of what would happen to those who dissent. But Farah couldnt recover from what happened, she still played dead under the bodies, breathing was almost impossible and the sounds of flies was sickening. 

[b]___________[/b]

[b]The Outskirts of Replazum, Pantagruel[/b]

The men rushed frantically through the forests, they had narrowly escaped the pursuit force but they needed to get out of the city now. 

After a couple hours of running, the group finally escaped Pantagrueli oversight, they set up camp in the Urglaaz swamp, which was commonly thought to be uninhabitable due to the dangerous fauna.

Within one of the camps was the leader of the Federalist Coalition, Saint Aerial, a born again priest who was denounced by the government for his anti-islamic speeches and call to an end to the Kim Dynasty; they wanted him dead.

A soldier bursts into the camp, panting frantically. Saint Aerial, we have terrible news.

[b]Yes, my child?[/b] 

The soldier turned his head to the ground and turned on the projector, he then inserted a tape and quickly rushed out the tent. 

Aerial expected it to be news about a military advancement but no, it was far worse. What he was about to see was the Bombardo incident. 2 minutes and 13 seconds, 2 minutes and 13 seconds of hell. Men, Women, Children, none were spared. Aerial felt as if he were going to vomit. This was something he never expected to see from the PRC, he just couldnt imagine it. But he had to silence his tears, this couldnt stand. Kim Jung Un must be punished for his sins.

Aerial emerged from his tent, grabbed a box, and rested one foot on it. 

[b]My brethren, the enemy grows stronger, more ruthless. They have crossed every line set by God, they treat their people like savages. I tell you this with all of my heart, this can NOT stand. We can not stand by and let them go after our wives, brothers, sisters, fathers, and kids! That is why we must keep fighting! No matter how big the sacrifice is, we must sacrifice our livelihood to rebuild what we lost. And usurp the devil from the throne, Kim must die!  DEUS VULT[/b]

[b]DEUS VULT[/b] His army said in unison.

Ragnorok has begun.
[/i][/spoiler]

[quote=shahzada;59908703][b]Question of the Day #194:[/b]

Nation Question: How would your nation handle this issue?

[i]This is an automated message.[/i][/quote]
There are no laws special to certain groups of people rather it is for all. Harassment, acts of violence, and inciting of violence is the same for all people under our nation. These are crimes and criminals will be equally punished according to the law. People often are bitter, and hateful, it does not matter your shade of person nor preference of partner, people will hate no matter the reason. The nation cannot ethically "change" individuals who are hateful to one group or another, what we can do however is curb this ignorance, by teaching all subjects without bias. 

Shielding those from knowledge does not provide them shelter, but strips them from it. It would be akin to taking fire away from the first of man, as fire is dangerous, but without it we would never progress.

Stachelland News Company - Insider, ep. 401. 'TRMS Jack Lennin finishes development.'
"This episode of SNC Insider will cover one of Stachelland's frigates, the TRMS Jack Lennin, about it, and an interview with the captain."

The TRMS Jack Lennin is the first of the Jack Lennin frigate class and is the first ship to be stored at Jack Lennin Maritime Base. Noticeably, both the naval institution and the ship share the name of Jack Lennin. The reason of the namings are due to tribute for the late Jack Lennin II, who was appointed the first Chief of the Stachelland Department of Defense, who, also, was widely considered as one of the best at his roles during his time. Lennin passed in 2010.

 - - - - - ERZA WHITE, ANCHOR, RENNY ZREPE, SHIP CAPTAIN - - - - -
E.W.: "In this short second-interview segment, I will be interviewing Renny Zrepe, the captain of the Jack Lennin, for a true insider look, so we can know a little about its history and capabilities."
E.W.: "Well, just as a starter, I have two questions for tonight. Do you have any previous relations to Jack Lennin, and do you think this ship is capable??"

R.Z.: "Well for your first question, a little bit. I mean, I met him twice in my early days as an officer candidate and non-commissioned officer when I received some medals. He was truly a kind guy, but I didn't really know him. I've heard great things, though. And, to answer your second question, absolutely. The front features a 120mm cannon and two 70mm cannons alone, all remotely controlled from the interior of the ship. Don't forget, it has two close-in-weapons-systems, or for those who don't know, they are used to shoot down missiles and nearby aerial threats, along with being capable of launching 6 surface to air missiles and 3 anti-ship missiles, it's dangerous, and it can hold a helicopter as well. It did cost some money though, that's for sure. From what I have heard, maybe 1.08 billion+, but its large price isn't just cannons, and close-in-weapons, it has some decent electronic warfare equipment and internals as well. And it doesn't just stop at this ship, this is only the first of its' kind."

E.W.: "Personally, when it was my time to serve my civil duty in the civilian military service almost every conversation mentioning him was compliments and admiring. A legend if I have ever heard. The Jack Lennin sounds like it will be a powerhouse, and the nation is excited to figure out when it'll be shown."
E.W.: "It was a great interview. This was Insider Episode 401 with Erza White."
